question.prompt:
On a checkerboard composed of \(64\) unit squares, what is the probability that a randomly chosen unit square does not touch the outer edge of the board?

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_8_Q10_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The checkerboard has \(8\) rows and \(8\) columns. A square avoids the outer edge exactly when it lies outside the first and last rows and outside the first and last columns.

Removing those rows and columns leaves \(8-2=6\) rows, each containing \(6\) eligible squares. Therefore there are \(6\times6=36\) eligible squares. All \(64\) unit squares are equally likely to be chosen, so the probability is
\[
\frac{36}{64}=\boxed{\frac{9}{16}},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
solutions.title: Count the interior squares
